sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever typed the same number over and over in your code? Named constants are here to save you! Let's learn how to make your code cleaner and easier to update.

• What named constants are and why they're awesome
• How to declare them using the `final` keyword
• Real-world benefits of using constants in your programs

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're baking cookies and the recipe says 'use 3.14 teaspoons of vanilla'. If you had to write that number 10 times, you might make a typo. Instead, you'd write 'PI_TEASPOONS = 3.14' at the top and just use PI_TEASPOONS everywhere.

That's exactly what named constants do in programming! They let you:

• Give a meaningful name to important values
• Use that name everywhere in your code
• Change the value in just one place if needed

Here's how you declare a constant in Java:

sections.title: 📌 The Syntax
sections.content:
```java
final double PI = 3.14159;
```

• `final` - This keyword makes the value permanent
• `double` - The data type (could be int, String, etc.)
• `PI` - The constant name (ALL_CAPS by convention)
• `3.14159` - The value that never changes

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Named Constants works:

steps.title: Without Constants
steps.description: You type the same value repeatedly, risking typos and making updates hard.

steps.title: Declare Constant
steps.description: Create a named constant at the top of your code.
steps.code:
final double PI = 3.14159;
// Now PI can be used everywhere!

steps.title: Use Constant
steps.description: Replace all hardcoded values with your constant. Update once, change everywhere!

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Must be initialized when declared (can't change later)
✓ Makes code more readable and maintainable
✓ Prevents magic numbers in your code

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use constants for values that appear multiple times
Place constants at the top of your class for easy access
donts: Don't use constants for values that change (use variables instead)
Don't forget to initialize constants when declaring
Don't use lowercase for constant names (against convention)
sections.protip: If you find yourself typing the same number more than twice, make it a constant!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Named Constants used in real apps?

examples.how: Use constants for tax rates, shipping costs, and discount percentages that need to be consistent across the entire application.
Use constants for gravity values, character speeds, and screen dimensions that remain constant during gameplay.
Use constants for mathematical values like PI, Planck's constant, or speed of light that never change.

problem.description:
Convert a temperature from Fahrenheit to Celsius. The formula is: Celsius = (Fahrenheit - 32) * 5/9. Your task:

1. Declare a constant for the freezing point of water in Fahrenheit (32)
2. Declare a constant for the conversion factor (5/9)
3. Calculate and print the Celsius equivalent of 98.6°F (should be 37°C)
hints: Remember to use ALL_CAPS for constant names
The conversion factor 5/9 should be stored as a double (5.0/9.0)
Use parentheses in your calculation to ensure correct order of operations
problem.explanation: By using constants, we make the formula more readable and easier to update. If the conversion factor ever changes (unlikely!), we only need to update it in one place.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Named constants make your code more readable and maintainable
📌 Always declare constants with `final` and ALL_CAPS names
📌 Use constants for values that appear multiple times or might change
📌 Practice declaring and using constants in simple calculations
📌 You're now ready to learn about data types and variables!
